The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

# Summary of Policy Document

This document outlines a comprehensive policy platform addressing multiple areas of governance, public services, and economic reform.

## Immigration and Border Control

The platform proposes freezing non-essential immigration while maintaining exceptions for healthcare workers. It advocates for offshore processing of asylum seekers, immediate deportation of foreign nationals who commit crimes, restrictions on student dependents, and a five-year residency requirement before accessing benefits. An employer tax of 20% on foreign workers is proposed to incentivise hiring domestic workers.

## Economic Policy

**Personal taxation** proposals include raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 annually, reducing fuel duty by 20p per litre, eliminating VAT on energy bills, cutting stamp duty on properties below £750,000, and abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million.

**Business measures** include exempting businesses with profits under £100,000 from corporation tax, reducing the main corporation tax rate to 15% over time, raising the VAT threshold to £150,000, abolishing business rates for high street enterprises, and introducing a 4% online delivery tax for large multinational companies.

## Public Services

**Healthcare** reforms focus on eliminating waiting lists through tax incentives for medical staff, utilising independent healthcare capacity, providing 20% tax relief on private healthcare, and implementing a voucher system allowing patients to access private treatment when NHS waiting times exceed specified limits.

**Policing and Justice** proposals include recruiting 40,000 new officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing, mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, building 10,000 new detention places, and reopening local magistrates' courts.

**Education** reforms propose curriculum changes emphasising national heritage, banning gender ideology teaching in schools, providing 20% tax relief on independent education, and scrapping interest on student loans.

## Energy and Environment

The platform advocates abandoning net-zero targets, scrapping renewable energy subsidies, fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licensing, exploring shale gas extraction, and developing nuclear energy through small modular reactors.

## Defence and Veterans

Proposals include increasing defence spending to 3% of GDP within six years, conducting an urgent military pay review, creating a dedicated veterans ministry, recruiting 30,000 full-time army personnel, and reforming defence procurement.

## Housing and Infrastructure

Housing measures include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping certain landlord tax restrictions, and protecting leaseholders. Infrastructure proposals include cancelling a major rail project, banning urban traffic restriction zones, and creating a new ownership model bringing 50% of utilities into public ownership.

## Agriculture and Fishing

Agricultural policy proposes increasing the farming budget to £3 billion, eliminating climate-related farming subsidies, and targeting 70% domestic food sourcing. Fishing reforms include ending automatic EU access to UK waters, requiring foreign vessels to purchase licences, and banning foreign supertrawlers.

## Constitutional and Social Reforms

Proposals include withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights, reforming the upper legislative chamber, restricting postal voting, considering proportional representation, replacing equality legislation, and reforming the national broadcaster's funding model.

## Financial Summary

The document claims potential annual savings of £150 billion through reduced government spending, benefit reforms, and energy policy changes, plus £10 billion from projected economic growth. Proposed spending increases total £141 billion annually, covering tax cuts, public services, and defence.

# Summary of 2024 Political Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a comprehensive policy platform focused on five key themes: economic fairness, public services, environmental protection, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economic Policy

The document proposes responsible fiscal management while investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. Key economic measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy to support high streets, expanding apprenticeships, creating Lifelong Skills Grants for adult education, and reforming parental leave. The manifesto emphasises supporting small businesses, entrepreneurs, and addressing the cost-of-living crisis through energy efficiency programmes and careful economic management.

## Healthcare and Social Care

Healthcare proposals centre on guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and ensuring NHS dental access for emergency care. Mental health receives significant attention, with plans for community hubs and school-based mental health professionals. The manifesto proposes introducing free personal care based on need rather than ability to pay, creating a Royal College of Care Workers, and establishing a cross-party commission on sustainable social care funding. Unpaid carers would receive increased support including paid carer's leave and respite breaks.

## Education

Educational priorities include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment features prominently, with additional free hours for disadvantaged children and increased Early Years Pupil Premium funding.

## Environment

Environmental commitments include achieving net zero emissions by 2045, generating 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030, and implementing emergency home insulation programmes. The manifesto strongly emphasises ending sewage pollution through transforming water companies into public benefit entities, banning executive bonuses until pollution ends, and replacing the current water regulator. Nature protection targets include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing

Housing proposals target building 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities and community-led development. Renter protections include banning no-fault evictions and creating three-year default tenancies. The manifesto commits to ending rough sleeping and abolishing residential leasehold.

## Crime and Justice

Policing reforms focus on restoring community policing, guaranteeing investigation of all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. The manifesto proposes tackling court backlogs, improving prison rehabilitation, and better supporting domestic abuse survivors.

## Immigration and Asylum

Immigration policy would transfer work visa decisions from the Home Office to relevant departments, expand youth mobility schemes, and reverse income threshold increases for family visas. Asylum reforms include processing claims within three months, allowing asylum seekers to work after three months, and establishing safe legal routes while working with European authorities to combat trafficking.

## Democratic Reform

Constitutional changes include introducing proportional representation for elections, lowering voting age to 16, capping political donations, and reforming the House of Lords. The manifesto proposes enshrining the Ministerial Code in law and creating a federal constitution with strengthened devolution.

## International Relations

Foreign policy priorities include rebuilding European relationships through a four-stage roadmap toward closer integration, supporting Ukraine, returning international development spending to 0.7% of national income, and advocating for a ceasefire and two-state solution in the Israel-Gaza conflict. Defence commitments include reversing army cuts and increasing spending toward 2.5% of GDP while maintaining nuclear deterrence.
